title: runtime-routing-sandbox-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for an engineering sandbox focused on runtime routing policies that balance latency, unit cost, and reliability across regions and instance tiers. The goal is a small, executable set of policy primitives + a decision tree that product/platform teams can iterate against with synthetic traffic before rolling rules into the control plane.

High-level goals and constraints:
- Goal: Keep 95th-pct latency within SLO for premium customers while minimizing per-token unit cost for background/batch workloads.
- Constraint: Some regions have limited dedicated capacity; fallback to cross-region increases tail latency but preserves availability.
- Constraint: Model variants (fp16/quantized) have observable differences in generation quality; quality regressions above threshold must trigger fallback to higher-quality variants.
- Non-goal: This sandbox is not the final policy language. It's an experiment space for tradeoff parameters and observable thresholds.

Policy primitives (small vocabulary used by decision tree):
- PRIORITY: premium | standard | background
- REGION: local | nearby | remote
- CAPABILITY: dedicated | shared | spill (burst)
- MODEL_TIER: high-precision | fast-quant | fallback-qa
- SIGNALS (inputs): live_p95_ms, queue_depth, capacity_util_pct, recent_error_rate, model_quality_delta
- ACTIONS: route(local, model), route(nearby, model), route(remote, model), throttle, queue, shed, notify-ops, switch-model, pin-route

Scoring function (single scalar used by tree edges):
- score = w_lat * normalized(latency_cost) + w_money * normalized(unit_cost) + w_rel * normalized(failure_risk) + w_qual * normalized(quality_delta_penalty)
- normalization: each signal scaled to [0,1] using rolling percentiles per-route (1h window) so we can compare different workloads.
- default weights (sandbox): w_lat=0.45, w_money=0.3, w_rel=0.15, w_qual=0.1. Weights will be swept in canary experiments.

Decision tree (textual sketch):
- Root: if PRIORITY == premium -> branch A else if PRIORITY == standard -> branch B else branch C

  Branch A (premium):
    if live_p95_ms < latency_target and capacity_util_pct < 80% -> route(local, high-precision)
    else if capacity_util_pct >= 80% and nearby has spare dedicated -> route(nearby, high-precision), notify-ops if cross-region=true
    else if recent_error_rate > 1% -> route(local, fallback-qa) and notify-ops; consider warm-up of dedicated nodes
    else if queue_depth > Q_THRESH and model_quality_delta < QD_OK -> burst-to-shared with model=fast-quant, set pin-route for 30s
    else -> route(remote, high-precision) with hedged request=disabled

  Branch B (standard):
    if score < score_threshold_standard_low -> route(local, fast-quant)
    elif score between low and high -> route(nearby, fast-quant) + enable batching-small (50ms window)
    elif model_quality_delta > quality_alert_threshold -> route(local, high-precision) but throttle to maintain SLO
    else -> route(remote, fast-quant)

  Branch C (background):
    if cost_savings_mode == true -> route(remote, fallback-qa) with large batching (200ms) and caching TTL=30m
    else if policy_max_latency < 1000ms -> route(nearby, fast-quant)
    else -> schedule-batch-run (defer 60s)

Notes on hedging and hedged policy:
- Hedging only for PREMIUM requests and only for short seq lengths (<256). Hedged candidate must be same model tier to avoid quality mismatches.
- Limit hedging concurrency to 1% of premium qps in the sandbox to avoid capacity amplification.

Quality gating and automated rollbacks:
- model_quality_delta is measured with a small, rolling prompt set per-route (100 examples); deviation measured with normalized BLEU/ROUGE-like metric + LM-estimated divergence.
- If quality_delta > 0.08 for >30 minutes after a model swap, auto-fallback to previous pinned model and create an incident stub (JIRA ticket template auto-created).

Simulation scenarios included in sandbox:
1) Regional outage in "nearby" region: synthetic spike of errors + capacity_util=100% in nearby. Validate that premium falls back to remote-only with acceptable SLO degradation (p95 growth < 2x).
2) Sudden qps burst from background workers: ensure background is throttled/queued and does not push shared capacity above 70% of premium capacity.
3) Quality regression in fast-quant variant: introduce model_quality_delta and verify auto-fallback and rollback behavior.
4) Cross-region cost shock: simulate increased egress costs; sweep weights to find w_money threshold where routing shifts to local despite latency penalty.

Control plane integration notes (how sandbox rules map to live):
- Policy definition format for sandbox: JSON-lite list of condition-action entries (easy to transpile). We will generate a compiler that outputs control-plane policy DSL.
- Each compiled rule emits telemetry hooks: routed_region, model_tier, decision_score, fallback_reason. These fields must appear in span/tags for tracing.
- Rollouts: support % rollout by traffic token, not by user, to avoid target leakage. Start at 1% for new policy weight sweeps.

Metrics and dashboards to create in sandbox:
- per-route: qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_depth, capacity_util_pct, recent_error_rate, model_quality_delta
- cost: tokens_consumed per-region, egress_bytes per-region, cost_per_1000_tokens
- policy effectiveness: fraction_routed_local, fraction_fallbacks, mean_decision_score
- alerting: premium_p95 > SLO*1.25 for 5m, premium_error_rate > 0.5% for 10m, model_quality_delta > threshold for 15m

Implementation caveats and TODOs:
- TODO: define Q_THRESH and score_thresholds per-service; start with conservative defaults for chat vs completion workloads.
- TODO: add live experiment for small voice assistant partner traffic (low-latency required) to validate hedging thresholds.
- Caveat: rolling percentile normalization can be noisy for low-traffic routes. Use hierarchical priors (global -> regional -> route) for stabilization.
- Caveat: switching model tiers frequently can cause cache churn (KV cache invalidation). Add a cooldown per-route (default 60s).

Open questions for architecture review:
- Should we expose routing score weights (w_lat, w_money, w_rel, w_qual) to customers on Dedicated? Pros: transparency for cost-aware routing. Cons: complexity and support surface.
- Cross-region egress costs fluctuate; do we incorporate real-time pricing signals or only daily cost signals?
- How do we reconcile model quality signal latency with strict latency SLOs? (quality evaluation is slower). Proposed: use fast LM-based quality estimate as proxy for quick gating.

Action items:
- [ ] Run the first weight sweep experiment across sandbox routes next week (owner: Luca).
- [ ] Draft a brief for private deployment teams describing differences in default weights and data residency constraints (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks to routing-proto PR (owner: Jonah).

Appendix: quick example rule (JSON-lite for sandbox)
{ "if": "priority==\"premium\" && live_p95_ms<350 && capacity_util_pct<0.8", "then": "route(local,high-precision)", "meta": "cooldown_s=60" }

End of doc. This is intentionally informal — use as a living sandbox.
